summary: June nonfarm payrolls came in at just 57,000, well below the 115,000 consensus, snapping a three-month run of stronger prints. Stock futures rose on the miss as traders eased rate-hike expectations, with the 2-year Treasury yield falling 3.5 basis points. Meanwhile, Fed Chair Warsh cited easing inflation risks tied to U.S.-Iran de-escalation talks, with WTI crude sliding to $67.59 as diplomatic progress continued.
tweet: June payrolls missed badly at 57K, cooling Fed hike bets and lifting equities — while U.S.-Iran talks kept oil falling and gold on the back foot heading into the holiday weekend.
